title: Strongest Chain
similar: LeetCode 124 Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum (general tree, parent-array input)
hints: A path in a tree goes up from one node to some highest node, then down to another. Which node is the highest one on the best path?
For every node, compute the best sum of a chain that starts at it and only goes downwards. A negative chain is never worth extending.

gain[v] = value[v] + max(0, best child gain). A path whose top is v is value[v] + the two largest non-negative child gains. Parents have smaller indices than children, so a reverse loop replaces recursion.

wrong.through_root.cpp: only considers paths whose highest node is the root
wrong.keep_negative.cpp: adds child chains even when they are negative
wrong.tle_every_start.cpp: walks the whole tree from every start node (fails the perf group)

strategy.question: Scout the statement: up to 2*10^5 nodes, values can be negative, a path may start and end anywhere, and a tree can be one long chain. Which plan fits?
options: Try every pair of nodes and add up the path between them
Run a search from every node and keep the best sum seen
One pass from the leaves up: each node's best downward chain, combined with its two best children at the top of a path
Sort the values and add the largest ones
strategy.why: Pairs and per-node searches are quadratic or worse, far too slow at 2*10^5 nodes. Sorting ignores that a path must be connected. A bottom-up pass computes, for each node, the best downward chain in O(children) and lets that node act as the top of a path, giving O(n) overall.
